findings.affected_surface: Backlog count semantics, BacklogEvent fields, countPollable, T6, and T14
findings.claim: FAIL: pending cannot simultaneously equal the number returned by poll_inbox and exclude replayed kinds. With 20 chat rows and one task_dispatch, the poll predicate returns 21 rows, but T14 requires pending=20 while also reporting the task_dispatch.
findings.evidence: Plan §2.1 says backlog.pending must equal what a subsequent poll sees and that backlog and pending_after share countPollable. Plan T14 instead requires pending=20 for 20 chat plus one task_dispatch. The current poll path fetches and ACL-filters all kinds without a kind exclusion.

findings.repair: Choose one invariant and encode it consistently. Prefer separate total_pollable and summarized counts: apply replay_max to summarized chat, keep pending_after as total pollable, and make by_kind totals reconcile explicitly. Update the event schema, T6, T14, and capped-count semantics.

findings.affected_surface: Cold-start threshold predicate and high-watermark selection
findings.claim: FAIL: the plan gives two incompatible cold-start populations. Section 2.1 requires the poll predicate, which includes delivered rows, while section 2.3 says a cold start operates only on delivered_at IS NULL rows.
findings.evidence: The existing cold-start drain calls fetchPendingSince, whose SQL requires delivered_at IS NULL. The poll path calls fetchInboxSince, whose SQL has no delivered_at predicate. Therefore a new connection with old globally delivered broadcasts can either trigger a large summary or see a small pending-only drain depending on which plan statement is implemented.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-09-15-replay-butler.md:45-51,86-88,143-144; packages/relay/src/messages/store.ts:170-185,198-214; packages/relay/src/routes/messages.ts:105-121
findings.repair: Define the cold-start decision population explicitly. If cold start intentionally reports all poll history, remove the pending-only claim and test a mixture of delivered and undelivered rows. If it remains pending-only, use a pending-only counter and stop claiming equality with poll_inbox for that case.

findings.affected_surface: Kind exemption policy for permission_verdict and task_result
findings.claim: FAIL: exempting only task_dispatch and permission_request suppresses their equally semantic completion kinds. A summarized permission_verdict never reaches the authorization tracker, and a summarized task_result never reaches dispatch correlation handling.
findings.evidence: InboundDispatcher performs authorization and terminal consumption for permission_verdict and correlation validation for task_result. poll_inbox only renders envelopes as text and does not execute either path. The plan says chat is the flood source but defines only task_dispatch and permission_request as always replayed.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-09-15-replay-butler.md:29-33; packages/peer-agent/src/inbound.ts:141-183,216-220; packages/relay/src/routes/permission.ts:54-65; packages/peer-agent/src/tools.ts:582-612
findings.repair: Make summarization an allowlist for chat rather than an exemption list, or at minimum also replay permission_verdict and task_result. Add tests proving these kinds still traverse InboundDispatcher when a chat backlog exceeds the threshold.

findings.affected_surface: Crash-safe ordering of backlog summary, exempt envelopes, durable cursor, and pendingBacklog
findings.claim: FAIL: no specified event order preserves both the cursor invariant and the promise that exempt rows are always replayed. Advancing the durable cursor to H before exempt delivery makes a disconnect lose every exempt row at or below H; delivering exempt rows first can advance the cursor past summarized chat before the summary and pending state are durable.
findings.evidence: The plan orders summary emission, cursorSink(newest), and pendingBacklog persistence as separate steps, while also requiring exempt messages within H to be replayed. Existing reconnects send the persisted cursor as since, and relay replay selects only id greater than since. InboundDispatcher advances the cursor after each accepted envelope.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-09-15-replay-butler.md:52-55,84-85,94-102,131; packages/peer-agent/src/index.ts:359-377; packages/peer-agent/src/inbound.ts:204-230; packages/relay/src/messages/store.ts:145-160; packages/peer-agent/src/cursor-store.ts:49-56
findings.repair: Specify a crash-safe commit protocol. For example, persist pending state before any cursor advance, deliver all exempt envelopes, then process an explicit completion event that atomically persists cursor H and pending state. Alternatively bundle exempt envelopes into a retryable backlog event and advance H only after every required final-mile delivery succeeds. Add disconnect tests at every boundary.

findings.affected_surface: poll_inbox pending_after parity for spool-enabled couriers
findings.claim: FAIL: leaving inbox-spool unchanged makes pending_after incorrect or unavailable for the poll-only courier that needs it. The merge can change next_cursor and truncate the union, while its return shape drops all response fields except messages and next_cursor.
findings.evidence: The current poll tool merges the relay page with local spool rows. mergeInboxPage may choose a cursor different from the relay cursor and returns only messages, next_cursor, and from_spool. The plan excludes inbox-spool from P4 even though agent-call poll-only deployments use that merged path.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-09-15-replay-butler.md:115-119,133; packages/peer-agent/src/tools.ts:582-610; packages/peer-agent/src/inbox-spool.ts:84-108; packages/peer-agent/src/outbound.ts:97-108; packages/peer-agent/src/index.ts:247-253
findings.repair: Bring inbox-spool into scope. Define whether pending_after counts relay rows or the merged inbox, preserve capped metadata through merging, and recompute remaining count relative to the cursor actually shown to the harness. Add tests with interleaved relay and spool rows that force truncation.

findings.affected_surface: pendingBacklog accumulation and clearing rules
findings.claim: The reminder state can forget an earlier unpulled batch: a second backlog event overwrites the single pendingBacklog object, and an unrelated poll whose cursor reaches newest can clear it without proving continuous retrieval from the stored since cursor.
findings.evidence: Section 2.4 assigns one pendingBacklog object from the current connection cursor and clears solely on next_cursor comparison. It does not define merging with an existing pending range or require the poll request to begin at pendingBacklog.since. The merged spool path can also produce a cursor different from the relay page cursor.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-09-15-replay-butler.md:97-105; packages/peer-agent/src/tools.ts:582-610; packages/peer-agent/src/inbox-spool.ts:101-108
findings.repair: Retain the earliest unresolved since value and extend newest when another batch arrives. Only reduce or clear state after a contiguous poll sequence anchored at that stored since, using the authoritative cursor for the counted source.

findings.affected_surface: Risk dispositions R-a through R-e
findings.claim: R-a requires pre-implementation definition because capped counting, complete high-watermark discovery, and aggregate statistics have different scan bounds. R-b requires a plan correction because from-based by_sender conflicts with T5 expecting an @team key. R-c is acceptable for v1 with the warning text, although meta.reply does not technically prevent an unthreaded response. R-d requires a strict synthetic-summary route because the current switchboard falls back to all registrations when a configured default target is absent. R-e may be deferred to telemetry because the threshold remains operator-configurable.
findings.evidence: The plan caps pending at 10000 but requires H to be the maximum matching id and does not define whether statistics cover the capped sample or the full set. It describes by_sender as senders but T5 uses @team. Current Switchboard.route returns all registrations if defaultTarget has no live match.

backlog_candidates.claim: The reminder state can forget an earlier unpulled batch: a second backlog event overwrites the single pendingBacklog object, and an unrelated poll whose cursor reaches newest can clear it without proving continuous retrieval from the stored since cursor.

R-a requires pre-implementation definition because capped counting, complete high-watermark discovery, and aggregate statistics have different scan bounds. R-b requires a plan correction because from-based by_sender conflicts with T5 expecting an @team key. R-c is acceptable for v1 with the warning text, although meta.reply does not technically prevent an unthreaded response. R-d requires a strict synthetic-summary route because the current switchboard falls back to all registrations when a configured default target is absent. R-e may be deferred to telemetry because the threshold remains operator-configurable.
